notes: 2025-11-20 - Created: inbound from product@billingsentinel.co; initial interest in hosted API for agent MVP.

Discovery 2026-01-12 (ff-2026-02-11-5781): spoke w/ Head of Product (Maya Lopez) + Eng Manager (Tom Reyes). Primary ask: replace rule-based scripts on support console with an LLM-powered assistant that can (1) triage billing questions, (2) propose exact Stripe/Zuora actions, (3) generate structured JSON for orchestration layer.
Use-case summary: mid-market billing support for 60k monthly invoices; live chat + async ticket triage. Expect ~50 concurrent agent sessions during peak; 1.4M monthly messages (est).

Latency SLO: must hit <= 250ms first-byte on streaming responses for chat starter messages; token-stream latency target <= 30ms per token under typical load. Customer emphasized UX: streaming + partial JSON for actions is critical.

Tooling requirements: function/tool-calling to call Stripe and Zuora APIs from assistant. Strict structured output: JSON schema validation required before action. Want Redwood's tool-calling + structured-output enforcement.
Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for console access, KMS integration for key material. Looking for audit logs per-request and retention controls (30/90/365 day options).

Initial path: start on Hosted API to iterate prompt + tool schemas, then move to Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation. Customer quote: 'Hosted is fine for staging, but we need Dedicated RU commitments before full rollout.'

Hosted POC 2026-02-07 -> 2026-02-28: ran a 3-week hosted POC using gpt-like open model in Redwood catalog. Worked through prompt-safety for refunds (sandboxed). Findings: streaming improved perceived latency but occasional token jitter at 95th percentile under load.

Demo notes 2026-02-25 (ff-2026-02-25-6142): demoed streaming + tool-calling; SE (Rohan) walked through field-level JSON outputs for 'create_refund' action via Stripe. Product team liked JSON enforcement but asked for stronger schema rejection semantics and guaranteed no hallucinated function names.
Performance benchmarks from Hosted POC: median first-byte 120ms, p95 first-byte 420ms under spike (50 concurrent). Main ask: reduce p95 to <= 300ms—this is why Dedicated is being evaluated.

Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget. They want guidance on Dedicated committed capacity vs. burst usage. Asking for cost model for 6/12 month reserved capacity with burst pricing and quantization/FP16 options.

Procurement & legal: legal flagged two items: (1) data residency wording around EU customers, (2) Dedicated breach notification SLA. Legal reviewing Redwood Dedicated contract; AVA following up with standard SAML + SOC2 artifacts (drive link).
POC plan for Dedicated (proposed):
- Week 0: sign POC NDA + infra checklist (VPC peering, routing, KMS key exchange)
- Week 1: deploy Dedicated instance in us-west-2, seed model variants (quantized + fp16), validate streaming endpoints
- Week 2: run synthetic load (50 concurrent chat sessions) + run tool-calling integration tests to Stripe sandbox and Zuora QA; capture token-level latency traces and cost per 1k tokens report.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 first-byte <= 300ms, successful sandbox tool-call rate >= 99% without JSON schema failures, cost projection within estimated ARR band.
Open technical questions raised by Eng Manager Tom:
- How does Redwood enforce structured outputs when model emits free text? Need strict schema validation and automatic fallback (reroute to human review).
- Can streaming responses include incremental JSON patches safely when actions require partial confirmation? (they prefer streaming + final JSON commit).
- KV-caching: customer asks whether billing entity lookups can be cached per session to reduce repeated embedding/lookup costs.

Sales/Commercial notes: proposed estimate sent 2026-03-03 (thread-Offer-2026-03-03-Ava). Price sensitivity around 'reserved capacity level 2' vs. 'level 3 burst'. Need to provide 12-month committed pricing and a 3-month pilot pricing.
CSM note: If POC passes, CSM (Clara) to run adoption plan with playbooks: 2-week enablement, prompt templates for refund flows, regression evals for hallucination metrics.
Blockers summary: legal sign-off on Dedicated contract, schedule pen-test for VPC, finalize pricing terms for reserved capacity.

Next immediate actions (owner tags): Ava -> deliver Dedicated POC runbook + pricing by 2026-03-12; Rohan -> provide technical run commands and sample tool schemas; Tom (customer) -> confirm sandbox Stripe + Zuora credentials and scope of actions allowed in POC.
Stakes: decision by 2026-04 if Dedicated delivers latency improvement + controlled cost. Strong chance to convert if p95 targets met and legal clears contract.
Longer term asks from product: offline auto-reranking for ticket-assignment, embeddings indexing for knowledge base, and cost-optimization recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
Internal notes: offer to include 2 weeks free burst credit for first-month Dedicated run to prove p95; legal to confirm if addendum needed.
